scenes.title: Eliminating Market Risk with Binomial Trees

beatOutlines.textOutline: A quantitative analyst introduces a one-step binomial tree where stock S0 = $20 moves up to $22 or down to $18 over interval T = 0.25 years ([fact-01], [fact-10]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The analyst explains how to form a riskless portfolio by taking a long position in Delta shares and a short position in 1 call option contract ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: By setting portfolio values equal in both up and down states, all market uncertainty is completely eliminated ([fact-02]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Display Delta calculation: spread in derivative payoffs ($1.00 - $0.00) divided by spread in stock prices ($22.00 - $18.00) equals Delta = 0.25 shares per option (25 shares per 100-share contract) ([fact-03], [fact-10]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Display risk-neutral pricing metrics at r = 12% and T = 0.25: exp(rT) = 1.03045, up probability p = 0.6523, yielding theoretical call price f = $0.633 per share ($63.30 per contract) ([fact-11]).

scenes.title: Deconstructing Delta and Risk-Neutral Probability Formulas

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Delta Formula: Delta = (fu - fd) / (S0*u - S0*d), representing option price sensitivity to underlying stock movements ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Risk-Neutral Probability and Pricing: p = (exp(rT) - d) / (u - d) and f = exp(-rT) * [p * fu + (1 - p) * fd] ([fact-06], [fact-07]).

summarySteps: 1. Binomial Stock Tree ([fact-01]): Stock price S0 moves up to S0*u or down to S0*d over interval T, with standard contracts representing 100 shares.
2. Riskless Hedging ([fact-02]): Combining a long position in Delta shares and a short position in 1 call option eliminates market uncertainty by equating portfolio values in both states.
3. Hedge Ratio Delta ([fact-03]): Delta equals the payoff spread divided by stock price spread: Delta = (fu - fd) / (S0*u - S0*d).
4. Risk-Free Return ([fact-04]): The hedged portfolio must earn the risk-free interest rate r: S0*Delta - f = (S0*u*Delta - fu) * exp(-rT).
5. Risk-Neutral Valuation ([fact-05]): Option prices derived by no-arbitrage do not depend on investor risk preferences or expected return mu.
6. Risk-Neutral Probability ([fact-06]): Artificial up probability p = (exp(rT) - d) / (u - d) aligns expected stock growth with the risk-free rate.
7. Theoretical Option Pricing ([fact-07]): The option price equals the discounted expected payoff in a risk-neutral world: f = exp(-rT) * [p * fu + (1 - p) * fd].
8. Arbitrage Enforcement ([fact-09]): Divergences between market option prices and theoretical price f enable arbitrageurs to lock in guaranteed upfront cash.
bottomTakeaway: The one-step binomial model demonstrates that option pricing requires no subjective risk preferences, using Delta hedging and risk-neutral probabilities p to enforce exact arbitrage-free valuations ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-05], [fact-07]).
